rodin.verdict: Closest balanced baseline in this run: readable eyes, wings, and tail with a restrained back. Smallest finished GLB.

seed3d.verdict: Front and rear stay close to the source. Good visual result at a lower listed price, but the delivered mesh is about 4.5× the Rodin file.

tripo.verdict: Recognizable face and wings at the lowest price. The GLB faces +X, so the viewer aligns it; 1.46 million triangles need optimization for mobile.

hunyuan-rapid.verdict: Fastest and lightest Atlas result. The face changes noticeably and the unseen back gains many spines, despite a mobile-friendly triangle count.

hunyuan-pro.verdict: Clean front silhouette, but softer source likeness and a heavily invented spiny back. Its 53.9 MB file is large for direct phone use.

hi3d-fast.verdict: Cute front with clear wings and tail; the rear invents large clustered spines. Two million triangles and a 4K map outweigh the small cost advantage.

hi3d-pro.verdict: Source-like front and complete wings, but a rear with enlarged decorative spines. Nearly two million triangles and 58.7 MB remain heavy for iPhone use.

hi3d-quality.verdict: Detailed front, but the unseen back adds prominent spines. An 8K color map and two million triangles make it a heavy export.

hi3d-master.verdict: More surface detail does not resolve the invented rear spines. At $5.185 and 115 MB, this run offers little app value over cheaper choices.

meshy-single.verdict: Readable front and complete wings, with extra spines on the unseen back. The 46 MB, 1.34-million-triangle GLB needs a mobile optimization pass.

meshy-multi.verdict: One-image output looks similar to Meshy single; this does not test true multi-view benefit. It is slightly heavier at the same listed cost.
